answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make every identity stake reputation earned through sustained, verifiable work, like a garden that only grows where real effort was planted. New identities start on a low ridge of trust with limited privileges and climb higher only after consistent honest behavior. Flooding the network then turns costly: an attacker riding a rising tide of fake accounts must still invest real work into each one, so mass identity creation stops being cheap and the economy stays anchored to proven contribution, not headcount.
